pages.title: celld Architecture
pages.purpose: Explain the overall system: the node/fleet model, cells as Durable Objects with per-cell SQLite, the bucket as root of authority, the clean-sheet decision core split between crates/logic and crates/celld, and end-to-end control/data flow.
instructions: Describe the workspace crate boundary and release build profile choices.
Document the clean-sheet boundary: crates/logic is a pure decision core with no I/O; crates/celld is the effect executor.
Explain the node-fleet-cell model and the bucket ownership mechanism.
Trace the actor serialization model and how events and effects flow.

pages.title: Change Guides for Representative Maintenance Tasks
pages.purpose: Focused, source-grounded guides for common maintenance tasks: changing a protocol/durability decision, adding a new Worker API surface, tuning presconcopic knobs, and operating a rolling upgrade.
instructions: Explain how a protocol change must be gated by the peer protocol version.
Explain how to add a new Worker API surface conformantly.
Guide readers to the pure decision core before the effect adapter for any behavior change.
Point to the simulation, model, and conformance layers that verify a change.

pages.title: Cloudflare Compatibility Boundary
pages.purpose: Document the Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects API surface celld implements, the supported Wrangler configuration subset, deployed services, and known compatibility gaps.
instructions: Catalog implemented vs partial vs unsupported services and APIs.
Document the Wrangler config keys celld accepts and rejects.
Explain the deployment feature gates and manifest schema.
Note silent-stub gaps as known exceptions.

pages.title: Durability, Fencing, and the Replication Protocol
pages.purpose: Document RPO=0 durability guarantees, epoch fencing, ownership records, node-log ensemble replication, the takeover recovery gate, storage requirements, and self-fencing.
instructions: Cover the LTX format and celld-ltx replication.
Detail the bucket requirements (conditional writes, read-after-write).
Explain self-fencing and the takeover recovery gate.
Explain the ownership record, epoch prefix, acknowledgement rule, and the fleet node-log ensemble.

pages.title: Limitations and Alpha Boundaries
pages.purpose: Document the alpha-era operational limits: single-application fleets, no TLS, plaintext peer traffic, storage credential requirements, WebSocket restrictions, and platform support.
instructions: Catalog the known limitations across fleets, networking, storage credentials, WebSockets, and platforms.
State uncertainty where the repository does not establish a fact.

pages.title: Fleet Operations, Diagnostics, and Configuration
pages.purpose: Explain operating a fleet: node leases, graceful shutdown and handoff, fleet readiness, operator CLI subcommands (diagnose, cell list, d1, kv, queue), environment variables, memory pressure, and deployment rollouts.
instructions: Document deployment adoption and the first-readiness gate.
Document node leases, drain token, graceful shutdown handoff, and rolling upgrades.
Document the operator CLI subcommands and internal operator API routes.
Explain memory pressure shedding and all the key environment variables.

pages.title: V8 Runtime, JS Embedding, and Application Execution
pages.purpose: Describe how celld embeds V8, runs Wrangler workers and Durable Objects, the isolate pool, the Durable Object storage/SQL interface, WebSockets, and worker features like cron, KV, Queues, D1, Workflows, R2, and Assets.
instructions: Describe isolate pooling with v8::Locker and the shared Worker queue.
Describe the reserved cells for D1, KV, Queues, cron, and Workflows.
Document the RuntimeManager lifecycle (start/publish/stop) and the actor lifecycle.
Document the cell storage (per-cell SQLite) and Durable Object storage API.

pages.title: Security Boundary
pages.purpose: Explain celld's security model: the trust boundary, the two listeners, the fleet HMAC peer authentication, the internal operator API authentication, request-body limits, and bucket credential handling.
instructions: Detail the fleet HMAC, clock limit, and replay protection.
Document operator API routes and their authentication.
Document the trust model (one fleet, one app) and external boundaries.
Explain the public vs internal listener split and the peer tunnel.

pages.title: Object Storage Backends and Bucket Contract
pages.purpose: Document the bucket abstraction across S3-compatible, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Blob Storage: conditional-write dialects, credentials, layout, prefixes, the storage probe, and the fleet key prefix.
instructions: Describe the two conditional-write dialects (S3 etag, GCS generation).
Document credential sources per provider (AWS chain, ADC, Azure families).
Enumerate the reserved bucket prefixes and the storage test.
Explain the fleet key prefix scheme.

pages.title: Telemetry and Observability
pages.purpose: Describe the optional telemetry system: Parquet-to-bucket sink, OTLP sink, the span/log schema, compaction, DuckDB querying, and configuration.
instructions: Cover the Parquet file format, partitioning, compaction, and DuckDB querying.
Document the bucket and OTLP sinks and all telemetry environment variables.
Explain the event schema and trace correlation.

pages.title: Testing and Verification Strategy
pages.purpose: Explain celld's multi-layer verification: differential conformance vs workerd, TLA+ model checking, deterministic simulation of the pure decision core, and live fleet fault injection.
instructions: Describe the four verification layers.
Document the fault-injection scenarios and the numbers the project trusts.
Explain the pure-decision-core design that makes simulation possible.

pages.title: celld Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical quickstart covering install, local development with celld dev, deploying an application, and running a fleet node.
instructions: Cover both local `celld dev` and a Cloud bucket fleet.
Describe the fastest path from clone to a running Worker.
List the exact commands for install, deploy, and node start.
